subject: English
central_question: How does Mr Lamb’s open, attentive way of living help Derry challenge the fear, alienation and self-hatred created by other people’s reactions to his scarred face?
in_scope_units: Before you read: the bond between an old man and a withdrawn boy.
Scene One: Derry enters Mr Lamb’s open garden and reveals his fear of other people’s judgement.
Mr Lamb’s garden, weeds, flowers, crab apples, bees, open windows and belief in the value of all life.
The contrast between Derry’s burned face and Mr Lamb’s tin leg.
Their discussion of beauty, listening, fear, friendship, isolation and personal choice.
Derry’s decision to return and Mr Lamb’s private sign of loneliness.
Scene Two: Derry resists his mother’s fear and chooses to go back.
Scene Three: Mr Lamb’s fall, Derry’s return and grief.
Reading with Insight Questions 1–4 and the alternative-ending activity.
banned_topics: A medical account of acid burns or prosthetic limbs beyond the play.
A clinical diagnosis of Derry’s mental state.
An invented continuation that is not clearly labelled as the textbook’s imagination activity.

known_pitfalls.claim: Mr Lamb pretends that Derry’s face is not scarred.
known_pitfalls.correction: He recognises the burn directly but refuses to treat it as the whole of Derry.

known_pitfalls.claim: Mr Lamb has no experience of physical difference.
known_pitfalls.correction: His real leg was blown off and children call him ‘Lamey-Lamb’.

known_pitfalls.claim: Derry changes only because Mr Lamb pities him.
known_pitfalls.correction: Mr Lamb does not pity him; he challenges Derry’s assumptions and emphasises choice, attention and participation.
He defies his mother, runs back and reaches the garden, but finds Mr Lamb after the fatal fall.

recommended_example_progression: Use Reading with Insight Q1 to explain what draws Derry to Mr Lamb.
Use Reading with Insight Q3 to examine alienation and the behaviour expected from others.
Use Reading with Insight Q2 to identify Mr Lamb’s loneliness and his ways of overcoming it.
Use Reading with Insight Q4 to evaluate the lasting effect of the meeting on Derry.
Use the How about activity only as an optional, clearly imaginative extension after mastering the given ending.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The play ends with Reading with Insight Questions 1–4 and a How about activity inviting students to imagine another ending.
